    AI Overview
    +13
    Effective customer feedback forms are short, specific, and goal-oriented. The best approach depends on your goal—ranging from a 5-question Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) Survey to single-question Net Promoter Score (NPS) polls. Always include open-ended fields and limit required questions to prevent form abandonment. 
    Here are highly effective examples tailored for different business needs: 
    1. Customer Service & Support
    Best used immediately after a help ticket is resolved or a customer service call ends. 
    • Overall Rating: "How satisfied were you with the support you received today?" (Scale: Very Dissatisfied to Very Satisfied)
    • Resolution Check: "Did we completely resolve your issue today?" (Yes/No)
    • Speed/Courtesy: "How would you rate the responsiveness and friendliness of our representative?" (Scale: Poor to Excellent)
    • Open Field: "What could our support team have done better?" (Multi-line text box) 
    2. Website & E-commerce
    Best used as a subtle pop-up on checkout pages or product pages. 
    • Ease of Use: "How easy was it to find exactly what you were looking for?" (Very easy, Easy, Neutral, Difficult, Very difficult)
    • Friction: "Is there anything stopping you from completing your purchase today?"
    • Navigation: "How was your shopping experience on our site?" 
    3. Physical Location / Retail Visit
    Best used on a tablet at the checkout counter or via a printed receipt QR code. 
    • Location: "Which store location did you visit today?"
    • Staff Attitude: "How would you rate the friendliness of our staff?" (Poor, Fair, Good, Excellent)
    • Environment: "How would you rate the cleanliness and organization of the store?" (Poor, Fair, Good, Excellent)
    • Open Field: "Do you have any suggestions for us?" 
    4. General Product / Post-Purchase
    Best sent via email 1-2 weeks after a customer has received their product. 
    • Value: "How would you rate the value for money of your purchase?"
    • Product Quality: "Which product feature do you like the most?"
    • Recommendation: "On a scale of 0-10, how likely are you to recommend our product to a friend or colleague?" (Standard NPS)
    • Open Field: "What features would you like to see us add in the future?" 
    To get started on building these for your own business, you can use customizable templates on Jotform's Feedback Categories or set up a quick questionnaire using Microsoft Forms Customer Survey. 
    If you tell me what type of business you run (e-commerce, software, physical restaurant, local service, etc.), I can help you draft the exact questions and best scales to use for your form.
